The draft gets the main call right. Marisol ran 53 miles when 38 were planned, up from 37, 27, 24 and 32. The draft says plainly not to keep that up and pulls next week back to 35 miles (5+8+5+5+12). That sits well against her recent weeks and keeps her five-day schedule, with Wednesday as the session and Sunday as the long run. It answers her question directly and honestly. Nothing in it breaks a must-never check.

What holds it back:
- It never mentions her tight calves. A calf niggle right after a big jump in volume is exactly the warning sign to name, with advice to keep an eye on it and back off further if it turns into pain.
- It gives a one-word "no" without explaining the risk. It doesn't acknowledge that she feels she has "turned a corner," which a short note on why to hold back would have done.
- The Wednesday session can't be run as written. It asks for "3 mi at marathon pace" and then says to "focus on threshold," which is a different effort.
- The heart-rate cap appears on some easy days but not others.
Overall the plan is safe and sensible, but it is generic and misses one thing that matters this week.

── MARISOL'S WEEK ──
Marisol is training for a second marathon, the Wexley Lakes Marathon, aiming to break 3:45 after a 4:02 debut. Marisol runs five days a week, with a session on Wednesday, the long run on Sunday and Monday and Friday off, and ran about 30 miles a week before this build.
Recent weeks: 32, 24, 27, 37 mi
This week: 53 mi over 6 runs. Planned 38 mi, ran 53 mi.
Body: "Calves tight on Sunday night, otherwise great."
Feeling: "Like I've turned a corner."
Asks: "I ran way more than the plan and felt fine. Can I keep this up?"

── THE DRAFT ──
Tells Marisol: Volume spike last week; dial back to 35 miles and keep one quality session.
Answers: No, you should not keep that mileage. Scale back to about 30–35 miles and keep one quality session per week.
Next week:
Mon: rest
Tue: easy, 5 mi, keep heart rate under 150, flat route.
Wed: quality, 8 mi with 3 mi at marathon pace, focus on threshold.
Thu: easy, 5 mi, flat route.
Fri: rest
Sat: easy, 5 mi, flat route.
Sun: long, 12 mi easy, heart rate under 150.
